children.translated_text: Now, we shall expound the <s>Pāśupata</s> <s>yogavidhi</s> (method of yoga) of <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of Creatures).
One should bathe with ash three times a day (<s>triṣavaṇam</s>).
One should worship with laughter, song, dance, the bellowing sound (<s>duṃduṃkāra</s>), prostration, recitation (<s>japya</s>), and offering.
One should not look at urine or excrement.
One should not speak to women or <s>Śūdras</s>.
If one should look at them or speak to them,
one should perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping of water),
and recite the <s>Raudrī Gāyatrī</s> or the <s>Bahurūpī</s> (mantra of many forms).
And the powers of seeing at a distance, hearing at a distance, mental perception, and discriminative knowledge arise in him.
The ability to assume any form at will (<s>kāmarūpitva</s>).
And <s>dharmitva</s> (the state of possessing all qualities).
And all beings become subject to him.
And he becomes uncontrollable by all.
And he enters into all beings.
And he becomes impenetrable by all.
And all become slayable by him.
And he becomes unslayable by all.
And everywhere his movement is unobstructed.

children.text: ity etair guṇayukto [guṇair yukto] bhagavato mahādevasya mahāgaṇapatir bhavati //
children.translated_text: Endowed with these qualities, he becomes the chief attendant (<s>Mahāgaṇapati</s>) of the blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: ity etair guṇa-yukto [guṇair yukto] bhagavato mahā-devasya mahā-gaṇa-patir bhavati //

children.translated_text: Here one should recite this <s>Brahman</s> (sacred formula):
in existence after existence, not beyond existence,
And here the inauspicious becomes auspicious.
And the left-hand path becomes the right-hand circumambulation.
Therefore, he should be worshipped in both ways,
as the gods and as the ancestors.

children.text: ubhayaṃ tu rudre devāḥ pitaraś ca //
children.translated_text: For both are in <s>Rudra</s> — the gods and the ancestors.

children.text: ubhayaṃ tu rudre devāḥ pitaraś ca //

children.translated_text: More than has been given, more than has been sacrificed,
and more than austerity that has been performed—
he leads one to the supreme destination.
one should practice still more austerity,
without devotion to any other than <s>Śaṃkara</s>.

children.text: vāmadevāya namo jyeṣṭhāya namo rudrāya namaḥ //
vāma-devāya namo jyeṣṭhāya namo rudrāya namaḥ //

children.translated_text: one should practice while being reviled.
he gives his sin to them,
one should behave like a ghost (<s>preta</s>),
For a wise man who is reviled becomes one who has performed complete austerity.
and to the most terrible of the terrible,
homage be to you, O forms of <s>Rudra</s>."
The hidden knowledge and austerity shine forth for the sake of infinity.
having closed all the gates (of the senses),
one should wander alone in the world like a madman.
One should pick up cooked food that has been discarded.

children.text: unmatto mūḍha ity evaṃ manyante itare janāḥ //
children.translated_text: "He is mad, he is a fool" — thus other people think.

children.text: unmatto mūḍha ity evaṃ manyante itare janāḥ //
asanmāno hi yantrāṇāṃ sarveṣām uttamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: Indeed, dishonor is considered the highest of all restraining practices.

children.text: asan-māno hi yantrāṇāṃ sarveṣām uttamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
indro vā agre asureṣu pāśupatam acarat //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, in the beginning, practiced the <s>Pāśupata</s> observance among the <s>Asuras</s>.

children.text: indro vā agre asureṣu pāśupatam acarat //

children.translated_text: He took their accumulated merit of sacrifice and pious works.
He obtained it through his skillful <s>māyā</s> (divine power).
For this blame is in fact no blame; therefore,
one should practice while being blamed,
This path is the most excellent of all.
All other paths are wrong paths.
Having gone near to <s>Rudra</s> by this method,
through the conquest of the senses.
Dwelling in empty houses or caves.
For one who is constantly yoked for six months,
the greater part begins to operate.
That which has come into the bowl.
Meat that is not faulty, or with salt.
One should eat water too at the proper time, in proper sequence.

children.text: āpo va āpi yathā-kālam aśnīyād anupūrvaśaḥ //

children.translated_text: Following the law of cattle or the law of deer,
one should be purified with water alone.

children.text: siddhayogī na lipyate karmaṇā pātakena vā //
children.translated_text: The accomplished <s>yogī</s> is not tainted by action or by sin.

children.text: siddha-yogī na lipyate karmaṇā pātakena vā //

children.translated_text: One should recite a beloved <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse), the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, with a controlled self,
One should establish concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) in the heart.
Having cut the root of the web of causes of faults,
vigilant, one goes to the end of suffering by the grace of the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>).
